scope: Package SPEC1 (TOOLS + DOCS only; no kernel, no web, no native build; Python 3.11, no network, NO MODEL CALLS - deterministic code). WHY: the owner has asked many times for 'a full specification'. A near-complete archive of his words EXISTS (docs/architecture/SLOWA_WLASCICIELA_2026-10-16.md: about 400 ids such as UI12, GR38, RE31, ON10, PC40 with verbatim quotes and a 'Sens:' line; docs/reports/LUKI_2026-10-16.md: about 380 ids with a status JEST / CZESCIOWO / BRAK / NIEAKTUALNE / SPRZECZNE, evidence and next step; docs/architecture/OWNER_REQUIREMENTS_2026-09-26.md: sections R1..R60 each with a verbatim quote), but it is prose in three files, stops being complete after 2026-10-16, and nothing consumes it: agent briefs are written by hand, so every owner correction becomes a restart. GOAL: make that corpus DATA with stable ids, so (a) a correction is one new or changed node, (b) briefs can cite node ids instead of pasting text, (c) the status of each item is visible, (d) nothing the owner said can be silently lost or paraphrased. BUILD, commit after each: (1) tools/spec.py with subcommands: `build` (parse the three files into docs/spec/spec.json, schema id loom.spec/1), `check` (consistency), `show <ID>` (a node with its verbatim quote, sense, status, evidence, source file:line), `list [--status S] [--theme T]`, `add` (append a NEW owner statement: --id R61 --date --quote-file F [--title] [--sense] -> writes the R-section in the OWNER_REQUIREMENTS format AND the node, refuses an id that exists, never edits an existing quote). (2) ID DECISION (owner asked 2026-10-23 'unikalny numer bez treści interpretowalnej?' - yes): the canonical id is OPAQUE, `s_` + 12 lowercase hex from uuid4 (the repo's id convention, see CLAUDE.md 'ID Generation'), carries no theme, kind or date - those are attributes; it is allocated ONCE and persisted in docs/spec/ids.json (alias -> id), `build` reads that registry and allocates only for items not yet in it, so a build with an existing registry is byte-deterministic, and correcting a transcription error in a quote (ASR mistakes happen) never changes the id. The historical codes (UI12, GR38, RE31, ON10, PC40, R56 ...) are kept as `aliases` (they are referenced all over the docs) and `show`/`list` resolve them; a brief may cite either, the canonical id is preferred. The node fields (examples of the shape, extend as the data needs): id, aliases[], understanding {text: the coordinator's PARAPHRASE of the requirement in its own words, state: proposed | approved | corrected, by, date, corrected_text} - owner rule R61 (2026-10-23): expensive work starts only after the owner approved the paraphrase, so the approval must be data, `spec.py approve <ID>` and `spec.py correct <ID> --text` record it, never auto-set, `list --understanding proposed` shows what still waits for him; the parser creates NO paraphrases (state 'none' for imported nodes) - paraphrases are written later by the coordinator, kind (requirement | rule | decision | question | philosophy - derive from the id prefix and the file, do not invent), title, date, quotes[] (verbatim, each with source file:line), sense (the 'Sens:' line when there is one), theme (the topic section of SLOWA the id sits in), status {value, checked_on: '2026-10-16', source: LUKI line} copied from LUKI and marked as a DATED OBSERVATION (owner rule R60: a fact about the present is a dated observation, never a constraint), evidence[], next_step, refs[] (ids mentioned inside the text), supersedes. Ids that exist in only one file keep their node with the missing parts null - nothing is dropped, items marked NIEAKTUALNE or SPRZECZNE stay with their reason. (3) `check` must verify: ids unique; every id in LUKI resolves to a SLOWA/OWNER node or is reported as an orphan with its line; every quote in spec.json is a verbatim substring of its source file (so a paraphrase can never be stored as a quote); counts per status and per theme; and print the list of ids present in one file and not the other (the coordinator measured: 403 ids in SLOWA, 382 in LUKI, 24 only in SLOWA, 3 only in LUKI - verify these numbers, do not trust them). (4) docs/spec/SPEC.md: a GENERATED view (header says so and how to regenerate) grouped by theme, each item one line with id, title, status and a link to the node; plus a top table of counts. Do not hand-write content into the generated file. (5) Tests: tools/tests/test_spec.py (unittest, no network): parse fixtures of each of the three formats (small synthetic samples that copy the real shapes), the verbatim-quote guard fails when a quote is altered, `add` refuses a duplicate id and leaves existing quotes byte-identical, build is deterministic given ids.json (two runs give identical bytes; a run without ids.json allocates and writes it). (6) Document in docs/spec/README.md in plain Polish (what it is, how a correction is recorded: `python3 tools/spec.py add ...`, how a brief cites an id) and add a decision entry 'S1 / SPEC1' to docs/reports/INDEX.md with how to reverse. EXAMPLES RULE (owner R58-R60, CLAUDE.md): everything concrete above (field names, statuses, themes, counts) is an example of the shape - design the parser around the real data, not around this list; if the real files contain ids, prefixes, statuses or sections not named here, include them; nothing is cut because it looks useless; report what the parser could NOT parse as a gap list in the card (do not drop it silently). The owner's private exports (docs/exports) and eval/real-holdout-key must not be read. Work in /home/user/chatadhd on branch claude/chataddhd-cpp-loom-core-IRGRN; other agents commit docs there too: `git add` only your own paths, retry if .git/index.lock exists, never force-push.

The card pastes: the counts, the number of items per status, the orphans, the unparsed gap list, and exactly what the coordinator must do to make briefs cite ids.
